new_statements.quote: La syllabe accentuée est, en règle générale, la première syllabe du monème. Les verbaux, en grande majorité monosyllabiques, [...] dans le syntagme verbal, cet accent ayant fonction contrastive, culminative que démarcative ; si le verbal a une forme redoublée [...], l'accent est sur la première syllabe. Dans les non-verbaux, [...] [monè]mes à initiale vocalique, et font exception également les monèmes A', pədao, "un champ", de plus de deux syllabes ayant pel ou kol pour première syllabe : tous ces monèmes sont accentués sur la seconde syllabe. Les monèmes monosyllabiques (A) (tels pād, "la case" ou ya, "ici") sont accentués dans le syntagme nominal [...]
new_statements.translation: The accented syllable is, as a general rule, the first syllable of the moneme. Verbals, mostly monosyllabic, [...] in the verb phrase, this accent having a contrastive [and] culminative rather than demarcative function; if the verbal has a reduplicated form [...], the accent is on the first syllable. In the non-verbals, [...] [mone]mes with initial vowel, and also excepted are the A' monemes [like] pədao 'a field', of more than two syllables having pel or kol as first syllable: all these monemes are accented on the second syllable. Monosyllabic (A) monemes (such as pād 'the house' or ya 'here') are accented within the noun phrase [...]
new_statements.citation: Ducos, Gisèle E. 1971. Structure du badiaranké de Guinée et du Sénégal (phonologie, syntaxe). Paris: SELAF (Bibliothèque de la SELAF 27-28). Phonologie §2.4 (accent).
new_statements.locator: Phonologie, §2.4 (continues into §2.5); page numbers not visible in Google Books snippet view (an adjacent snippet on syllable structure carries '2.72 70', so the accent section lies around pp. 68-72, unverified)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ducos describes Badiaranke as a language without tones with an intensity accent that falls, as a general rule, on the first syllable of the moneme (lexical morpheme/word): verb stems, mostly monosyllabic, are accented in the verb phrase, reduplicated verb stems on their first syllable; nouns and ad-nominals on their first syllable, except vowel-initial ones and trisyllabic-plus stems beginning pel-/kol-, which are accented on the second syllable. Monosyllables take the accent within the phrase; grammatical monemes generally have no accent of their own, but the class determiner is always (weakly) accented and within a phrase a further accent falls on the third syllable after the last accented lexical moneme.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Snippet: 'le monème déterminant de classe (b"') fait exception en étant toujours accentué, mais cet accent peut être dit secondaire parce que d'intensité moindre, une intensité "normale" n'étant perçue pour ce monème qu'en fin de syntagme'; also 'la troisième syllabe suivant la syllabe accentuée du dernier monème énoncé ayant un accent propre' is placed under accent in the NP or VP (rhythmic accent at phrase level).
new_statements.exceptions: Vowel-initial monemes and >2-syllable monemes beginning pel-/kol- are stressed on the second syllable; preposed (B)/(D) grammatical monemes are unaccented except the pronominal D' paradigm; for certain (D) pronominal monemes presence vs absence of accent is distinctive, separating 1sg from 3sg ('deux monèmes (D) de même articulation s'opposent par la présence ou non de l'accent qui distingue ainsi 1ère et 3ème pers. sing.'); an 'accent d'insistance' (emphatic accent) is mentioned in the syntax.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the moneme (Martinet framework) inside the nominal or verbal syntagm; accent is intensity-based; résumé states the language is 'sans tons'. Quote assembled from Google Books snippet-view fragments (ellipses mark snippet boundaries; 'guera'/'sée' scanned garbage omitted); the book itself was not opened and page numbers are unverified. Cover 2010: 5 warns that Ducos's phonological description is 'misleading in many respects' and that her minimal pairs are single syllables never spoken in isolation.
new_statements.identity_note: Ducos 1971 describes Badiaranke of Guinea (Koundara area) and Senegal (Casamance/Velingara); Cover 2010 is based on Paroumba (Senegal) and Sounkoutou (Guinea); Wilson 1984/2007 'Pajade' is the Guinea-Bissau variety. All fall under bady1239 (no dialect glottocodes).

sources.citation: Wilson, W. A. A. 1984. Biafada, Pajade, and the 'Polyglotta'. Journal of West African Languages 14(2): 61-80.
sources.note: Silent on stress: sections on consonant mutation, vowels, noun classes, verbal system and Koelle comparison; the only 'accent' mentions (pp. 71-72) concern Koelle's diacritics in the Polyglotta ('Koelle's use of accents is hard to account for. They are ignored here').

sources.citation: Cover, Rebecca Tamar. 2010. Aspect, Modality, and Tense in Badiaranke. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. ix+277 pp.
sources.note: Silent: no phonology chapter; no statement on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the 291-page text (only 'stresses' as a verb). pp. 5-6 review prior descriptions and say Ducos 1971 is 'misleading in many respects, in both the phonological and syntactic domains', and that the New Tribes Mission phonetics/phonology sketch (companion to Brown & Logdon 1994) is unpublished.
Nothing on phonology; Glottolog adds Westermann 1921 and Koelle 1854 to the seven refs in the target record.
